flawed_step: Step 1: with five neighbours and four colours, exactly one colour appears twice. Say v1..v5 in cyclic order get 1,2,3,4,2. A (a,b) swap on a component K removes colour a from the neighbours only if K holds every a-neighbour and no b-neighbour. Step 2 fails: it claims planarity guarantees that some pair (a,b) and component K meet this condition. Planarity only stops chains of disjoint colour pairs from crossing. Here the chains v1–v3 (colours 1,3), v1–v4 (1,4), v2–v3 (2,3), v4–v5 (2,4), v3–v4 (3,4) and v1–v2 (1,2) can all exist without crossings, so every swap is blocked. This is Kempe's gap at degree 5.
counterexample:
Start with the wheel: v joined to v1..v5, plus the rim cycle v1v2v3v4v5. Colour v1..v5 with 1,2,3,4,2. Outside the rim, add the path v1–y–z–v3 with y=3, z=1, running on the v2 side. Also add the path v1–w–u–v4 with w=4, u=1, running on the v5 side. The graph is planar, simple, and G−v is properly coloured with all four colours on the neighbours. Components that contain a neighbour, and the result of swapping each one:
(1,2): {v1,v2,v5} gives 2,1,3,4,1.
(1,3): {v1,y,z,v3} gives 3,2,1,4,2.
(1,4): {v1,w,u,v4} gives 4,2,3,1,2.
(2,3): {v2,v3} gives 1,3,2,4,2; {v5} gives 1,2,3,4,3.
(2,4): {v4,v5} gives 1,2,3,2,4; {v2} gives 1,4,3,4,2.
(3,4): {v3,v4} gives 1,2,4,3,2.
Every result still uses all four colours. Swapping a component with no neighbour of v changes nothing on the neighbours.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. This is Kempe's flawed argument for degree-5 vertices. The explicit planar graph above, with its colouring, is blocked for every pair of colours: no single Kempe-chain swap leaves only three colours on v's neighbours. The claim that some single swap always works therefore fails.
